newsitem.title: USA: Key U.S. lawmaker urges early U.S. Bosnia pullout.
newsitem.headline: Key U.S. lawmaker urges early U.S. Bosnia pullout.

text.p: House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich said on Sunday he would press to bring home by Spring U.S. troops in the planned NATO follow-on peacekeeping force in Bosnia rather than let them stay the 18 months President Clinton has proposed.

Kasich, appearing on the NBC television programme "Meet the Press," said he feared that the United States was on its way to becoming a permanent military presence in Bosnia, equating it with the 45-year U.S. stay in South Korea.
Kasich, a Republican from Ohio, said he planned to work with a bipartisan group in Congress to shift more of the peacekeeping burden to European countries.

He said Clinton's plan to keep a reduced U.S. force in Bosnia for 18 months "a big mistake." Though he conceded U.S. troops should not withdraw immediately, Kasich said his "sense" was that they should be home by this spring.
"We did our job over there. It's now up to the Europeans to exercise real burden-sharing and American forces ought to come home in a timely manner," he said.

"I am very very concerned this could represent a permanent presence in Bosnia, like we've had in Korea. I think it would be a major mistake. And I think that the risks to our troops over time is too high, and it is not in the vital American interest," he said.
